tagline: Tokyo's nearest sea escape — the city already flies to its islands above the waves; it's time the ride went clean, quiet and reliable.
summary: The Izu Peninsula and the Izu Islands are Tokyo's closest marine playground: the hot-spring and beach towns of Atami, Ito and Shimoda along the Sagami Bay coast, and the volcanic islands of Oshima, Niijima and Hachijojima out in the Pacific. Atami alone draws 5M+ visitors a year. The islands are already served by high-speed jetfoils that literally fly above the waves — Japan has accepted foil-borne sea travel for decades — but the fleet is ageing and weather-fragile. This is a mature commuter-and-leisure corridor on Tokyo's doorstep ready for a clean, quiet, reliable next generation across two distance bands.

demand_signals.label: Atami visitor volume
demand_signals.note: Tokyo's nearest hot-spring resort city, ~50 min by Shinkansen; strong domestic and growing inbound demand on the Sagami Bay coast.

demand_signals.label: Existing foil-borne ferry market
demand_signals.note: Tokai Kisen runs high-speed jetfoils from Tokyo (Takeshiba) to the Izu Islands — passengers already understand and value flying above the chop.

demand_signals.label: Ageing / weather-fragile fleet
demand_signals.note: The island line-haul is reliability- and comfort-constrained on rough days — a clean, modern foiling replacement closes the gap.

demand_signals.label: Tokyo-metro proximity
demand_signals.note: Atami–Ito–Shimoda strung along the peninsula, with Sagami Bay sheltered and the open Pacific island runs longer — a natural two-band network.

demand_signals.label: Premium hospitality anchor
demand_signals.note: Design-led luxury on the peninsula with no premium on-demand sea transfer to or between properties and islands.

use_cases.title: Clean next-gen island line-haul
use_cases.body: Modern, quiet foiling service on the established Tokyo/Atami ↔ Izu Islands corridor — replacing the retiring jetfoil generation with a reliable, comfortable, lower-emission ride on a market that already exists.

use_cases.title: Sagami Bay coastal hopping
use_cases.body: Smooth all-electric hops along the peninsula — Atami, Ito, Shimoda — and out to Izu Oshima, letting Tokyo weekenders chain beach and hot-spring towns without the train backtrack.

use_cases.title: Resort & island private transfers
use_cases.body: Direct foiling arrivals to resort and island jetties (Amanemu, Shimoda, Oshima) — one seamless premium hop instead of train-plus-ferry-plus-shuttle.

use_cases.title: Far-island hybrid connection
use_cases.body: The longer Pacific runs to Niijima and Hachijojima exceed all-electric range — a Quanta-LR hybrid corridor that links the outer Izu Islands with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

journeys.with_navier: A smooth, near-silent all-electric foiling hop straight to the island from the hot-spring coast.

journeys.today: Slow coastal rail or winding road down the peninsula; no fast sea link between the resort towns.
journeys.with_navier: A coastal foiling chain stitching the hot-spring and beach towns together over calm Sagami Bay water.

journeys.today: Ageing jetfoil ~2h20m, or an overnight large ferry; comfort and schedule both fall apart on rough days.
journeys.with_navier: A clean, modern foil-borne crossing on the corridor Tokyo already rides — quieter, smoother and lower-emission (near the all-electric range edge; Quanta-LR for full reliability margin).

journeys.with_navier: A Quanta-LR hybrid line-haul reaching the far Izu Islands with no charging stop required.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Sagami Bay coastal band is Pioneer II territory: Atami–Ito–Shimoda hops and the Atami ↔ Izu Oshima crossing (~13 nm) sit well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on relatively sheltered water. The Tokyo ↔ Izu Oshima run at ~65 nm is near the all-electric range edge — workable as Pioneer II in good conditions, but a candidate for Quanta-LR reliability margin (flag for a coordinate check before it becomes a marquee routed edge).
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The open-Pacific runs to the outer islands — Niijima (~80 nm) and Hachijojima (~155 nm) — exceed all-electric range and are Quanta-LR hybrid corridors, ideal for resurrecting the long island line-haul with no charging-infrastructure dependency on remote volcanic islands.

competitive_landscape: The corridor is served today by Tokai Kisen (high-speed jetfoils and large ferries from Tokyo Takeshiba to the Izu Islands) and the Tokyo-Wan ferry, plus coastal sightseeing boats along the peninsula. The existing jetfoil service is itself the demand evidence — Tokyo has ridden foil-borne sea travel for decades — but the Boeing 929 generation is ageing, weather-fragile and comfort-limited. A clean, modern, reliable foiling fleet modernises an adopted habit rather than creating a new one; that is the opening.

precedents.why_it_matters: Decades of foil-borne ferry service prove passengers already value flying above the chop; the clean, quiet, reliable next generation is a natural upgrade, not a behaviour change.
A $100M, ~100-vessel phased electric-foiling network shows the two-platform model at national scale — the playbook to replicate for a coast-plus-islands geography like Izu.

seasonality: Sagami Bay's inner coast (Atami–Ito–Shimoda) is relatively sheltered, but the open-Pacific runs to the Izu Islands are exposed and see winter NW winds and the summer typhoon window (roughly Aug–Oct), when the ageing jetfoils are slowed or cancelled. Foiling's smoother ride above the swell is exactly the comfort-and-reliability premium that the current fleet cannot deliver on rough days.
regulatory_note: Operates under Japan Coast Guard (JCG) and MLIT Maritime Bureau oversight, spanning Shizuoka Prefecture (peninsula) and Tokyo Metropolitan Government (the Izu Islands sub-prefecture) — a cross-prefecture jurisdiction. Much of the coast and islands lies within Fuji-Hakone-Izu National Park. Aligns with Japan's 2050 carbon-neutrality and MLIT zero-emission-vessel programmes; replacing the ageing diesel/turbine jetfoil generation is a concrete clean-fleet modernisation angle.
signature_routes: Atami ↔ Ito ↔ Shimoda (Sagami Bay coastal chain, all-electric)
Atami ↔ Izu Oshima (sheltered island crossing, all-electric)
Tokyo (Takeshiba) ↔ Izu Oshima (jetfoil-corridor modernisation, ~65 nm — near range edge)
Tokyo / Shimoda ↔ Niijima / Hachijojima (outer-island hybrid line-haul, Quanta-LR)
